note: Page (Bulletin July 17, 1918) prints a Fuel Administration Zone A coal order signed by Garfield that only cites the August 23, 1917 Executive order; nothing on Hot Springs hospital rations.
Page carries a Fuel Administration Iowa coal order effective July 1, 1918, gold statistics and a State Department directory; no order placing public health activities under the Treasury.

Page (Bulletin August 21, 1918) prints a Fuel Administration anthracite lake-dock order citing the August 23, 1917 Executive order and bid notices dated August 23, 1918; no Klamath River allotment order.
Date match comes from the 1917 Fuel Administrator appointment citation and August 23, 1918 bid openings; no Virginia Key reservation order on the page.
Page holds a Fuel Administration coal order, a Postmaster General notice and bid notices; no revocation of E.O. 2168 or Stanislaus lands order.
Page (Bulletin August 24, 1918) has congressional summaries, supply proposals and the start of a Fuel Administration price order citing the 1917 Executive order; no Oregon land withdrawal.
War Industries Board is mentioned only in congressional news; no order adding a WIB representative to the War Trade Board appears on the page.
Page (Bulletin August 27, 1918) prints Fuel Administration lake-forwarder charge rules where June 1, 1918 is a period boundary; no Bar Harbor port of entry order.
Page (Bulletin September 21, 1918) prints a Fuel Administration cement fuel regulation whose base period ends December 31, 1917; no order relating to Indians on the public domain.
Date match is a Fuel Administration tipple-coal order dated August 16, 1918 signed by Garfield; no Lituya Bay timber reservation order on the page or the next.
